content.title: Anne Teresa De Keersmaeker at the Zurich Theaterspektakel: Dancing to the Songs of Jacques Brel
content.lead: The great Belgian choreographer explores the songs of the legendary chansonnier together with young artist Solal Mariotte. Their togetherness becomes a separation – as if a mother had to let go of her son.
content.author: Lilo Weber

image.author: Simon Aurel Schwarz / ZTS
image.caption: Dancing as if they were simply enjoying life: Solal Mariotte and Anne Teresa De Keersmaeker in «Brel.»

content.caption: Dancing as if they were simply enjoying life: Solal Mariotte and Anne Teresa De Keersmaeker in «Brel.»
content.author: Simon Aurel Schwarz / ZTS

content.text: Is it magic? Coincidence? Or both? The ship appears on the lake stage at the Zurich Theaterspektakel at exactly the right moment. Flames flicker across the back wall of the stage. Jacques Brel sings of great love, but the people freeze. For they have only themselves to embrace. They stand there lonely, their hands wrapped around their own bodies, staring into the fire on the wall.

Then the «Linth» sails across the lake through the sea of flames and, as its schedule commands, docks in front of the Landiwiese. «E la nave va» (And the Ship Sails On) – a Fellini-esque moment for this homage to the great Belgian chansonnier: «Brel» by Anne Teresa De Keersmaeker and Solal Mariotte. And a moment that brings another image to mind: how Pina Bausch once stood as the blind Princess Lherimia at the railing of the luxury liner that Federico Fellini sent on a collision course with a cruiser in 1983.

The association is not far-fetched: the older Anne Teresa De Keersmaeker gets, the more she physically resembles the icon of dance theater – but she creates a completely different dance. And she can legitimately be called the Pina Bausch of new Belgian dance, as she, along with Alain Platel, Jan Fabre, and Wim Vandekeybus, initiated the Flemish wave during the 1980s that changed Western dance forever.

She has remained the most influential of the four because she tirelessly creates and has reinvented herself and her dance several times. But also because her school P.A.R.T.S., founded in Brussels in 1995, has shaped generations of lively dance artists. One of them is Solal Mariotte, with whom Anne Teresa De Keersmaeker stands on stage in «Brel»: he is 25, she is 66. He is a breakdancer. She remains the dancer of clear steps and forms, as we came to know her when she first came to Zurich in 1983.

At that time, she danced «Fase, Four Movements to the Music of Steve Reich» (1982) with Michèle Anne De Mey, and the eponymous piece «Rosas danst Rosas» (1983) with her newly founded company Rosas. It was immediately clear that something entirely new was happening here, a new relationship between dance and music.

image.author: Simon Aurel Schwarz / ZTS
image.caption: Three generations: Solal Mariotte, 25 years old. Anne Teresa De Keersmaekersie, 66 years old. And in the background, Jacques Brel (1929–78).

content.caption: Three generations: Solal Mariotte, 25 years old. Anne Teresa De Keersmaekersie, 66 years old. And in the background, Jacques Brel (1929–78).
content.author: Simon Aurel Schwarz / ZTS

content.text: In seemingly constant, repetitive patterns, «Fase» moves through changes in the tempi of phase shifts in Reich’s early compositions «Piano Phase» (1967), «Come Out» (1966), «Violin Phase» (1967), and «Clapping Music» (1972) – with mathematical rigor.

Minimalism and repetition are revisited in «Rosas danst Rosas» to music by Thierry De Mey and Peter Vermeersch, albeit emotionally underpinned by the intense dance of the four women. Both pieces have remained in the Rosas company’s repertoire and have been performed hundreds of times. «Rosas danst Rosas» over 500 times, danced by 28 different dancers. And now the production is touring in its fifth generation – also through Switzerland in November. Zurich, therefore, witnessed a piece of dance history at the Theaterspektakel in 1983.

Some in the audience on the Landiwiese this evening may remember this. Anne Teresa De Keersmaeker had not been seen here for a long time. Now the grand dame of Belgian dance is back on stage with her usual presence, between the generations: Solal Mariotte (born 2001) and Jacques Brel (born 1929). The way the songs about love and death are explored is certainly unusual. At times, Anne Teresa De Keersmaeker follows the bass line, the rhythm of the chanson, while Solal Mariotte does his breakdance thing on the floor, taking more and more liberties as the evening progresses.

Sometimes they meet in the melody. But both also engage with the content through their movements or imitate the singer’s delivery, for example, practicing his pathos. They also fool around, as an old couple for instance in «Les vieux» (The Old Ones). One has not seen such things from Anne Teresa De Keersmaeker before. As if the artist, whom we know as a strictly formal, rather austere performer, would simply let form be form for once and enjoy the rest of life.

image.author: Simon Aurel Schwarz / ZTS
image.caption: Sometimes De Keersmaeker and Mariotte fool around on stage.

content.caption: Sometimes De Keersmaeker and Mariotte fool around on stage.
content.author: Simon Aurel Schwarz / ZTS

content.text: «Brel» begins in «Le Diable (ça va)» (The Devil (It's Okay)) with old age. Only gradually do the dancers emerge from the shadows. To «Sur la place» (In the Square), De Keersmaeker begins to shrug her shoulders slightly, swing her hips, and venture first steps. From somewhere, Solal Mariotte shouts into the chanson «Quand on n’a que l’amour» (When We Only Have Love), as if making fun of the elderly.

Waltzes are danced, and movements from «Violin Phase» and «Piano Phase» from «Fase» are quoted. The blazer is thrown to the floor, and clothes are even taken off entirely. The initial togetherness becomes a separation, as if a mother had to let go of her son. Finally, they lie down on the floor and leave the stage to Jacques Brel: «Six pieds sous terre, Jojo, tu n’es pas mort. Six pieds sous terre, Jojo, je t’aime encore.» (Six feet under, Jojo, you are not dead. Six feet under, Jojo, I still love you.)
«Rosas danst Rosas» can be seen on Nov. 25 at the Théâtre Les Halles, Siders, and on Nov. 27 and 28 at Nebia, Biel.

metadata.nzzSummaryEN:
- Anne Teresa De Keersmaeker and Solal Mariotte reinterpret Jacques Brel's songs through a blend of dance and theater, merging generations and dance styles.
- The performance "Brel" at the Zürich Theaterspektakel explores themes of love and loss, incorporating humor and showcasing a more playful side of the choreographer.
- The production stylistically references De Keersmaeker's earlier works while her collaboration with Mariotte introduces new creative dynamics.
metadata.nzzSummaryDE: - Anne Teresa De Keersmaeker and Solal Mariotte interpret Jacques Brel's songs with a blend of dance and theatre, bringing together generations and dance styles. - The piece «Brel» at the Zurich Theatre Festival explores love and loss, incorporates humor, and reveals a new, playful side of the choreographer. - Stylistically, the production draws on De Keersmaeker's earlier works, while the collaboration with Mariotte introduces new creative dynamics.
